title: Chilaquiles Red Salsa

description: Chilaquiles Red Salsa is a beloved Mexican breakfast dish, perfect for a flavorful start to your day. This recipe features crispy tortilla chips generously coated in a homemade, spicy red salsa, creating a comforting and satisfying meal. Often garnished with fresh cheese, crema, and a fried egg, it offers a delightful balance of textures and tastes.

ingredients.notes: plus more for frying chips if homemade

instructions.title: Prepare Vegetables for Salsa Base
instructions.text: In a medium saucepan, combine the roughly chopped tomatoes, Serrano chiles, 1/4 medium white onion, and peeled garlic cloves. Add enough water to cover the vegetables. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce heat and simmer for about 10-12 minutes, or until the tomatoes are soft and their skins begin to split. Drain the cooking water, reserving about half a cup.

instructions.title: Blend the Red Salsa
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked tomatoes, chiles, onion, and garlic to a blender. Add 1 cup of chicken broth (or water) and 1 teaspoon of salt. Blend until completely smooth. If the salsa is too thick, add a little of the reserved cooking water until it reaches your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Fry the Salsa
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Once hot, carefully pour the blended salsa into the skillet. Be cautious as it may splatter. Bring the salsa to a simmer, stirring occasionally, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing it to thicken slightly and deepen in color. Taste and adjust salt if necessary.

instructions.title: Prepare Tortilla Chips
instructions.text: While the salsa simmers, if using homemade tortilla chips, fry them until golden and crispy, then drain excess oil and season with salt. If using store-bought chips, ensure they are fresh and crisp.

instructions.title: Combine Chips and Salsa
instructions.text: Once the salsa has thickened, add the 8 oz of tortilla chips directly into the skillet with the hot salsa. Gently toss the chips until they are evenly coated. Do not overmix, as you want the chips to retain some of their crunch, but be thoroughly covered in the delicious sauce. Cook for just 1-2 minutes until heated through.

instructions.title: Serve and Garnish
instructions.text: Immediately transfer the chilaquiles to individual serving plates. Garnish generously with a drizzle of Crema Mexicana, a sprinkle of crumbled Cotija cheese, fresh chopped cilantro, and thinly sliced red onion. For a heartier meal, top each serving with a freshly fried egg. Serve hot and enjoy this authentic Mexican breakfast.

tips: For a deeper, smoky flavor, lightly char the tomatoes, chiles, onion, and garlic on a comal or cast-iron skillet before boiling. This adds a fantastic layer of complexity to your salsa.
Adjust the heat level by increasing or decreasing the number of Serrano chiles. For a milder salsa, remove the seeds from the chiles or use fewer. For a spicier kick, add an extra chile or two.

Serve chilaquiles immediately after coating the chips in salsa to prevent them from becoming too soggy. If you prefer a bit more crunch, you can serve the salsa on the side and let people add it to their chips.
